payload.claim: No test exercises the branch of `if current and current not in recorded:` where `current` is non-empty AND *is* in `recorded` — i.e. a second push_unpackaged_work call over a branch this same spec already pushed (a retry after a rate limit, per the spec's own SA-0031/gotcha framing). Every test in `packageable` pushes onto a fresh remote (`current == ""`), and the one test with a pre-existing remote branch (`test_unpackaged_work_does_not_replace_a_branch_someone_else_moved`) deliberately keeps it unrecorded so the refusal fires. Replacing the condition with `if current:` (always refusing whenever the branch exists, dropping the `recorded` carve-out) keeps every existing test green — including the 'someone else moved' test, which still refuses — while silently breaking the documented ability to overwrite one's own prior unpackaged push on retry.
